name: Sacre-Coeur
_about: THE BASILICA OF SACRE-COEUR, Montmartre (Abadie, 1875-1914), Romano-Byzantine in white travertine, on its real plan (OSM building parts, Wikipedia): the Greek cross of four barrel-vaulted, gabled arms round the 16 m crossing, PENDENTIVES carrying the great drum of sixteen windows, the gallery storey with its open arcade and the tall ribbed egg dome with its colonnaded lantern and cross (~87 m); the four corner towers over sail-vaulted bays, each with its octagonal drum, small egg dome and lantern; the low aisles round it under flat roofs; the long choir, the APSE with its half dome (the mosaic of Christ in Majesty), the ambulatory and six half-domed radiating chapels; the square CAMPANILE behind (the axial chapel at its foot, the Savoyarde in its belfry, a small dome and cross); the three-arched PORCH with the bronze equestrian statues of Saint Louis and Joan of Arc, the Sacred Heart on the gable, the parvis and its flight; the CRYPT under all of it. A stair turret in the back west angle climbs to the high terraces, the gutter walks lead to the deck round the drum, and a second turret against the drum to the outer and inner GALLERIES at the dome's foot.

crossing piers._about: the four piers of the crossing, 2.85 m square, from the crypt to the roofs: the great arches and the pendentives stand on them

nave east wall._about: the nave arm's side walls, 2.85 m: an arch into the corner bay under its small dome and one into the aisle beyond; the crypt's arches under them

front wall._about: the front: three doors from the porch into the nave, the great window over the porch's roof, the gable over it all

east transept front._about: the transepts' fronts: two tall windows, and the rose in the lunette under the barrel

arm barrels._about: the barrel vault over each arm, from the crossing (its first bay the great arch) to the arm's end

pendentives._about: the pendentives turning the crossing's square into the drum's circle, and the deck round the drum's foot: the roof walk between the four arms' gables

nave roof._about: the arms' gabled roofs in stone, from the drum's deck out to the gables; between their eaves and the wall heads' outer edges the gutter walk

front east corner side._about: each corner tower's two outer walls: a great arch into the aisle beyond, blind over the aisles' roofs

corner vaults._about: the sail vault over each corner bay

corner towers._about: the corner towers' masonry over their vaults, up to the terrace the small domes stand on

small domes._about: the four small domes over the corner towers: an octagonal drum with an arch in every face, the ribbed egg dome, the lantern and its cross (OSM: drums to 33 m, domes to 46 m, lanterns to 53 m)

dome._about: the great drum, sixteen tall windows over the roofs, the egg dome on its gallery storey with sixteen ribs, the colonnaded lantern, ball and cross (OSM: the dome 50-73 m, the lantern to 83 m)

gallery storey._about: the drum's gallery storey under the dome: a window in every bay but one

gallery storey door._about: ...and the door from the outer gallery to the inner one

inner gallery._about: the inner gallery round the drum's foot of the dome, 54 m over the church's floor

outer gallery._about: the outer gallery round the drum, walked behind its arcade (the stair turret stands in one bay of it)

gallery arcade._about: the open arcade round the outer gallery, its sills the parapet

gallery roof._about: the cornice over the arcade, the gallery's ceiling: the dome stands behind it

gallery interior._about: the gallery storey's space, up to the dome's springing

dome stair._about: the stair turret against the drum, over the south-west crossing pier: from the deck round the drum's foot up to the outer gallery

east front aisle front._about: the aisles' outer walls, from the ground to their flat roofs: tall round-headed windows, the crypt's small lights under them

east aisle roof 1._about: the aisles' flat roofs, over their ceilings

east choir aisle terrace._about: the choir aisles' upper masonry behind the back corner towers (OSM's 24 m block), its top a terrace walked from the stair turret to the gutter walks and round the apse

apse crypt._about: the apse's wall in the crypt, arched into the crypt's ambulatory

apse arcade._about: the apse's arcade into the ambulatory, an arch a bay

apse upper wall._about: the apse's wall over the arcade, up to the half dome

apse half dome._about: the apse's half dome, its crown the choir barrel's: inside, the great mosaic of Christ in Majesty

apse roof._about: the half-cone stone roof over the apse, to the choir roof's ridge

ambulatory vault._about: the ambulatory's barrel vault, round the apse

ambulatory upper._about: the masonry over the ambulatory's vault (the gallery storey of OSM's 24 m ring)

ambulatory roof._about: the ambulatory's flat roof, walked round the apse

ambulatory wall._about: the ambulatory's outer wall: an arch into each chapel (and in the crypt, into the crypt's chapels under them)

ambulatory crypt floor._about: the floor of the ambulatory and the apse over the crypt

crypt chapels._about: the crypt's six chapels under the church's

chapels._about: the six radiating chapels round the ambulatory, each a half round of windows under its stone half dome (the seventh, the axial one, is the campanile's foot)

chapel floors._about: the chapels' floors over the crypt's

campanile._about: the campanile's square shaft: the axial chapel at its foot (the arch from the ambulatory), the long shaft of paired lights, the open belfry

savoyarde._about: La Savoyarde, the great bell (18.8 t, 3 m across), hung in the belfry

campanile buttresses._about: the buttresses at its corners, running up into pinnacles

campanile stage._about: the arcaded stage over the belfry

campanile dome._about: its little drum and egg dome, the lantern and the cross

campanile interior._about: the axial chapel in the campanile's foot

porch floor._about: the porch's floor, a step over the parvis

porch arcade._about: the porch: three round arches on the parvis (after Saint-Front at Perigueux)

porch roof._about: the porch's roof, a terrace behind its balustrade

porch balustrade._about: the balustrade along the porch's roof

statue piers._about: the porch's corner piers, rising over its roof to carry the two equestrian statues

statue plinths._about: the statues' plinths, run forward of the piers clear of the turrets behind

saint louis._about: the bronze equestrian statues by Hippolyte Lefebvre on the porch's corners: Saint Louis to the west (left as one faces the front), sword raised

joan of arc._about: Joan of Arc to the east, sword raised

facade turrets._about: the slender turrets either side of the gable, their small domes over the roof's eaves (OSM: 33 m)

sacred heart niche._about: the aedicule on the gable, the Sacred Heart standing before it (OSM: 35.5 m)

sacred heart._about: Christ of the Sacred Heart blessing, over the front

parvis._about: the parvis before the porch, a terrace over the hill on blind arches

porch steps._about: the steps from the parvis up to the porch

great flight._about: the broad flight from the hill up to the parvis

roof stair._about: the stair turret in the back west angle, its door to the west at the ground: 156 steps up to the high terraces, its belvedere and cone over them

roof stair bridge._about: the bridge from the turret's door over the aisle's roof to the choir aisle terrace

church floor._about: the church's floor over the crypt

crypt piers._about: the crypt's piers under the church's floor

crypt interior._about: the crypt: the church's plan a storey down

church interior._about: the church up to the aisles' roofs: the cross, the corner bays, the aisles, the choir aisles and the ambulatory (the chapels' and the apse's own above)

nave interior._about: the arms over the aisles' roofs, under their barrels, to the pendentives' ring
